t.E527.agn: In 1965, JECFA set the ADI for ammonia solution (ammonium hydroxide) as 'not limited'; the evaluation stated that no toxicological reason was seen to limit use in line with good manufacturing practice, but that the total ammonium intake from these additives should be kept in mind from a nutritional point of view. In the EU it is a Group I additive; EFSA's re-evaluation has not yet been published (it was included in a call for data in 2016).
t.E527.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E527.prod: It is produced chemically by dissolving in water ammonia obtained from the catalysed reaction of hydrogen with nitrogen.
t.E527.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E527.regx.2: Included in the call for use/concentration data as part of the re-evaluation (deadline 31.01.2017).
t.E527.summary: Ammonium hydroxide. Used as an acidity regulator in cocoa and some other products.
t.E527.what: It is an aqueous ammonia solution used to regulate acidity and to neutralise. In food it reacts with acids to form ammonium salts.
